items.title: Kerala High Court moots lowering juvenile age from 18 to 16 years
items.summary: The Kerala High Court has observed that legislatures should consider reducing the age threshold for juveniles and children in conflict with the law from 18 to 16 years. Hearing a writ petition on Friday, November 13, 2026, the court said present trends indicate that children attain sufficient maturity by the age of 16. Justice A Badharudeen expressed concern over the easy availability of liquor to minors, observing that the issue requires detailed consideration in view of recent fatal accidents allegedly caused by persons below 18 years of age after consuming alcohol. Kollam-based journalist Vinod Vikraman Pillai had filed a petition alleging liquor was being sold to people under 23 years of age, violating Sections 15A and 15B of the Kerala Abkari Act. In its order dated November 13, the court noted that the petitioner's principal grievance was the alleged failure to enforce these statutory provisions, despite the restrictions imposed by law. items.title: Andhra secures Rs 9.98 lakh cr worth of investment proposals at CII Summit 2026
items.summary: Andhra Pradesh has secured investment commitments worth Rs 9.89 lakh crore at the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Partnership Summit held in Visakhapatnam on November 12 and 13, Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu said. He also said that the state government would provide clearances for industries in real time with self certification to encourage investors. Naidu also announced that the proposed ‘Investors Protection Act’ will be enacted with retrospective effect from 2024 to allay fears of investors during change of governments. The legislation will reportedly include provisions to ensure that any approvals granted to investors by an administration cannot be revoked when a different party comes into power. CM Naidu had on November 12 said that investors coming to the state had many doubts about “regime change” and had suffered because of “vindictive politics.” Speaking to media persons after the conclusion of the summit, the Chief Minister said Andhra Pradesh had attracted investments worth Rs 9,88,957 crore through 303 Memoranda of Understanding (MoUs) at the event.
